recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Further changes to the custodian/contributor/author distinction should be new Patient Care work, not a remaining application step for FHIR-7069.
issue_request: FHIR-7069 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for DSTU1 CarePlan.Author. It asked whether the author was always the party responsible for the plan and resolved to amend the wording to identify responsibility for the contents of the plan.
initial_application: SVN r6766, imported as git commit d6c4981fa8fe7d58cc3e1cc393aa8cc0b6a83c54, changed the then-current CarePlan.author short label from 'Who is responsible for plan' to 'Who is responsible for contents of the plan' in source/careplan/careplan-spreadsheet.xml.
additional_context: CarePlan remains active in source/fhir.ini, but the current source no longer has CarePlan.author as a same-name element. Later Published issue FHIR-28544 renamed author to custodian and updated the model so custodian is responsible for the care plan while contributor identifies who provided the contents. Later no-change issue FHIR-33954 confirmed that a plan author/lead-development concept is contributor semantics, not custodian semantics. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-7069 found no conflicting community decision record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already conveys the semantic distinction that matters for implementers, and changing CarePlan.custodian to responsibility for contents would conflict with later published decisions.

related_jiras.note: Published R5 issue renamed CarePlan.author to custodian and explicitly set the current custodian and contributor definitions.
Resolved - No Change issue confirmed that author/plan-development wording belongs to CarePlan.contributor rather than custodian.
